title: Rabbi Abbahu (Yuchasin Notice)
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Yuchasin cites “Rav Ada and Rava bar Chanan came to him” in chapter Makom SheNahagu. [Seder HaDorot](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=113&lang=en) writes: “I have not found it.” Hyman locates the story in [Pesachim 51a](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.51a.9) in the Dikdukei Soferim reading. Hyman says the Rif reads “they came and said to Abbahu”; Yuchasin read “to Rabbi Abbahu.” The Rif and Ran reading “to Shmuel’s father” is, in Hyman’s judgment, a printing error. Hyman argues that the correct reading must be Rav Avya Saba (Rav Huna’s student, as in [Beitzah 21a](https://www.sefaria.org/Beitzah.21a.2-3)) and Rabbah bar Rav Huna came and spoke to “his father,” meaning Rav Huna.[^1]

notes.text: Heilprin quotes Yuchasin and says he did not find the case. The consulted [Rif, Pesachim 17b](https://www.sefaria.org/Rif_Pesachim.17b.2) gives Rav Avya and Rabbah bar Chanin reporting to Shmuel’s father. Hyman treats the last words as a printing error. The consulted Pesachim instead names Rav Avira Saba and Rabbah son of Rav Huna reporting to Abaye. Beitzah places Rav Avya Saba in discussion with Rav Huna. Hyman’s alternative readings and account of the printings remain his.
